shared_elements: frontal anthropomorphic head carved in coarse stone
banded headdress/cap covering upper part of head
projecting ears at sides of head
eyes rendered as simple carved slits/lids
rounded monolithic block form with flat-ish frontal presentation
justification: Both are frontal, blocky stone sculptures whose upper zone is occupied by a horizontally banded headdress or cap sitting above a broad face with slit eyes and side ears, so the vertical ordering of headgear-over-face corresponds closely. The differences are large, however: A is a tall full-figure monolith whose body carries shallow incised discs, bands and abstract motifs, rendered in thin linear engraving on smooth dark stone, whereas B is an isolated head modelled in bold rounded volumes on granular pale stone with a distinctive gridded, bared-teeth mouth that has no counterpart in A.
